headline: Enhanced sampling and ensembles resolve conformational distributions of proteins and RNA
label: Conformational Ensembles And Dynamics
summary: Multithermal and crystallographic ensemble methods now tie conformational sampling to experimental NMR, SAXS, and ITC observables.
synthesis: The common thread is the replacement of single-structure descriptions with conformational distributions, quantified through enhanced sampling, multiconformer models, and learned surrogates. OPES multithermal sampling in one replica yields atomistic IDP ensembles that match REST2 and NMR/SAXS data, revealing transient tertiary structure in ACTR. A benchmark on an RNA tetraloop identifies T-REMD as the most robust of the enhanced-sampling methods tested for RNA folding free-energy estimation. Multiconformer crystallographic ensembles estimate protein and solvent conformational entropy from X-ray structures and predict ITC binding entropies. Deep GIST predicts hydration energy, entropy, and free energy distributions around proteins in seconds rather than hours. What is new is that ensemble-derived quantities, including conformational entropy and hydration thermodynamics, are being tested directly against experimental binding and structural data.
